{{Short description|American physicist}}
{{BLP sources|date=March 2019}}
'''Thomas Joseph (Tom) Bowles''' is an American [[nuclear physics|nuclear]] [[physicist]] who works at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lanl.gov/collaboration/fellows/fellows-biographies.php|title=Fellows Biographies|first=Los Alamos National Laboratory, Operated by Los Alamos National Security, LLC, for the U. S. Department of|last=Energy|website=www.lanl.gov}}</ref>  He served as the Laboratory's Chief Science Officer from 2004 to 2006, and also was science advisor to [[New Mexico]] Governor [[Bill Richardson]] from 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abqjournal.com/news/state/apscience07-05-06.htm|title=ABQJOURNAL: Gov. Richardson Names Science Adviser|website=www.abqjournal.com}}</ref>

Bowles received his [[B.Sc.]] degree at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder|University of Colorado]] in 1973 and his [[Ph.D.]] at [[Princeton University]] in 1978. He joined the Physics Division at Los Alamos in 1979 and was named a Fellow of the Laboratory in 1994.

He was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 1992 <ref>{{cite book|title=Los Alamos Science|page=91}}</ref> and awarded the M. A. Markov Prize by the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]' Institute for Nuclear Research in 2003.
